title: What If Sound Could Travel Through Space? You'd Hear the Sun

scenes.text: What if sound traveled through space? You'd hear the Sun, and it would arrive years late.
Today it can't. Sound is vibrations passed between particles, and space has almost none to carry them.
At the 343 meters a second that sound moves in air, the Sun's roar would need roughly 14 years to arrive.
You could not hear it anyway. Sound waves bounce across the Sun in about two hours, far too low for ears.
Scientists speed the recordings up 42,000 times, squeezing 40 days of vibrations into a few seconds, to make them audible.
So the Sun does sing. Its surface rises and falls about every five minutes, a note far below human hearing.
